Self-aware but not self-indulgent, heavy but meaningful and using repetition in a correct way, that is how I would describe Red Haze. This might be my favorite RPG maker game to date. It shows how despite having limitations in budget, it still delivered a great experience by making the most out of their creativity and limited resources. It is one of those games that you either love or hate. So, if this sounds like something up your alley, please try it.

Before continuing, a short stop to reiterate a massive trigger warning. This game very openly deals and shows violence, drug use, nudity, sexual assault, prostitution, homelessness and many more heavy topics. I’m of the mindset that Yai Games tackled these topics with respect but still.

This game tells its story with the premise that it will be played several times and made the most out of that. In theory each playthrough can be different, showing you new sequences and getting new endings. In practice you will get stuck and you will endure frustration, but just enough to immerse you in the mindset of the main character. Every time you make progress it feels meaningful and usually progress comes in chunks, with several roads opening at the same time. It uses repetition in a way that has meaning for the experience they are creating and it kept me engaged thanks to that. Still this is one of those aspects that you either love or hate, so keep this in mind before you buy the game.

The tone of the game is a balance between creepy, depressing and funny. Usually at least two of those emotions are present at every moment creating a rather unique game. Although, one thing that can take you out of the experience is that for several endings you must get the main character nude and control her like that. Personally I didn’t find it to be meaningless but my wife didn’t agree, feeling it was a bit too voyeuristic without much reason.

The art style is a very interesting aspect as it was what motivated me to play the game but also was one of the things that almost made me stop playing the game. All the scene illustrations are very well done, delivering on the emotions they should and without being exploitative of the characters. On the other hand, many of the sprites and animations feel way more rough, which at the start pulled me out of the game. In the end I thought the concept was interesting enough and ignored those thoughts of stopping. Funny enough, the more I played, the more I enjoyed the art in the game. It feels very unique to it and also shows how the developer did everything they could to make this game a reality, even if something wasn’t their forte.

I love this game and hope it reaches all the people that are looking for this very unique type of experience.

Red Haze, oh boy where do I start?

For as much as I like the atmosphere and creepiness of this game, I sadly can't say I'd recommend it. For starters it isn't finished, in the sense not all of the endings are in the game nor do I have hope that they will be. So as of this review, you can't fully complete this game and get what I'm assuming would be the true end. I think this a case of being a little too ambitious with all the endings (there's supposed to be 26, one for each letter of the alphabet). 
Edit 1: Currently as of editing this there are 4 endings that are missing from the game so some achievements are not possible to get (despite the fact Steam says 0.6% of people have those particular ones).

I just want to get this point of the way now and just say that this game is kinda too difficult to play. I'm not talking in sense of the gameplay mechanics but more of how you get the endings. Some are easy, you just go through and do your base goal. Then others are basically impossible without some kind of guide or lots of trial and error. 

Edit 2: After going through the game some more and being able to get a total of 11 endings, I believe the previous point still stands. This game requires a lot of trial and error as I've already stated. Guides have been helping me through some points of the game but honestly gameplay videos and written walkthroughs are rather sparse so it's been quite the task. I want to continue to try and get at least a few more endings but I don't know know if I'll be able to get all of the currently available ones.

[spoiler]One particular ending is linked to the creature in the well and being able to successfully play through a game of hide and seek, failing to find said creature within the allowed time will automatically be a fail and you will get one of the other endings. This is a clever way to make the player tense when trying to find the creature as it's within a maze, but if you don't take a very specific path, you will not find it and therefore always fail. The time you're given it just that tight. Not an enjoyable experience.[/spoiler]

As for the puzzles, well let's just say they vary from fairly easy to figure out to down right headache inducing. You may even get different puzzles during separate playthroughs depending on which key you are given near the start (it can be one of three and it's dictated by how observant you've been) so certain endings are only available with certain keys. Don't get me wrong, I do enjoy the challenge but some of these puzzles are really just left up to guess work.

[Spoiler]I think one of the best examples I've experienced and remember was the puzzle related to the abomination in the underground dungeon. There is three points on that part of the map that have electrifyable floor panels with switches. You have to lead the abomination to each of these panels and shock it. The catch being, you only have one chance to get it. Also, if you die to it you have to use one of the adrenaline to revive yourself. When I first went to this area I didn't know about the abomination and when I found one of the panels, I immediately used the switch, not realising what it was. The game then doesn't really tell you that you have to go to a generator to charge the panel again (I believe this may be the case for each panel), I then found the abomination but then remembered the panel, so I led it over there, to then find out that it didn't work anymore and then died. I ended up giving up on that playthrough cause I wasn't sure what I was supposed to go or do and wasted about 2-3 hours of work. What I learnt for this? Red Haze needs to have better sign posting to let players know if they're doing something right or wrong, if even just a little bit.[/spoiler]

This is just one thing players will become accustomed to when playing Red Haze, the other is the player character's stamina bar. It is so small. You are not able to sprint for that long and normally that wouldn't be so bad, this is a horror game after all, but there's just one little factor that makes this more frustrating than anything. The Janitor. Ah yes my favourite character, the Janitor. This guy can move the same speed as your sprint but he never has to stop for a breather, making him a pain to maneuver around cause as soon as he sees you, that's it and he'll make a b-line for you. Get caught and it's into the well with you. Though after being caught a certain amount of times you'll get the option to use an adrenaline to get rid of him for the rest of that playthrough. But hey, that's great right? Well not exactly. You see the adrenalines are limited and once you've found and used them all there's no more in the entire game. That means certain endings will become impossible to achieve if they require at least one adrenaline.

[spoiler]Edit 4: Once I completed Ending V in the well (it's the one you get from the arcade machine) the janitor has been changed permanently to now make things harder. Before I could use the adrenaline to poof him away for the rest of that run but now I can no longer do that. On top of that, he's now able to enter rooms when I'm in there.[/spoiler]

Any who, rant aside, final thoughts time. Red Haze had potential to be rather great, the developer clearly shows that they can do good sound design and there is a genuine mystery in this game that I would love to see resolved by the end but with how things are right now, I don't see that happening. Even though I said I don't recommend this game, I can see why some people may like it and in a way, I kinda like it too despite all the flaws.

Edit 5: I just want to add this onto the end but after getting some very helpful unlocks in the game [spoiler] the fairy outfit and teal key shortcut [/spoiler], some stuff has become a little easy, especially in terms of travel. I think I have become more neutral on the game and less negative leaning, I might even go as far as to say I'm starting to lean a little to the positive but I think my original rating still stands as of now.

As of 2021, within two months of its final update, I find myself greatly surprised by Yai Gameworks spirit in general and Red Haze. Duskgolem, depicting a great knack for showmanship, enjoys engaging with its niche audience in many different ways, and loves making each individual experience unique and even exclusive at times.

This pholosophy is better seen in Red Haze, an apparently generic RPG horror game that doesn't mind holding back a lot until you're really engaged with it. The more endings you get, the more the game plays a masterful dance of streamlining boring events and making chill events difficult or tense. The element of permadeath and what "continue coins" that disappear permanently from the game after being picked up, Surprise encounters that are triggered on rare ocassions each run, and some game overs being but the tip of a thread to yet more discoveries.

These are just some examples to what makes Red Haze a truly special game that really grows on you the more you play it, the more you explore it. Even if its tone can be a bit overly angsty at times, the honesty, bluntness and passion with which it delivers itself will be something you'll draw charisma from. A game I truly recommend despite its traditionally unfair design at times. But that it's appropiately on it for the show.

[h1] 좋은 아이디어, 부족한 실행력 [/h1]
개발자의 전작인 Close Your Eyes를 인상 깊게 플레이했기에, 유료인 이건 더 다양한 컨텐츠가 있겠거니 하고 구매한 게임이다.

물론... 더 다양해지긴 했다. 엔딩이 8개인 Close Your Eyes와는 달리, 26개의 엔딩, 더 다양한 맵과 숨겨진 요소들이 있고, 더 다양한 아이디어들이 사용되었으며, 공포 쯔꾸르의 기본 덕목인 묘하게 기괴한 요소와 좋은 퍼즐들도 (많지는 않지만) 있다. 특히 3D 미로를 구현한 맵에서는 감탄하기도 했다.

하지만 문제는, 이 좋은 아이디어들을 디자인이 따라가지 못한다는 것이다. 우선, 인터페이스가 별로다. 주인공의 기본 이동 속도는 너무 느린데, Shift로 스프린트를 할 수 있지만, 얼마 지속되지 않아서 뛰었다 걸었다를 반복하게 된다. 만약에 짧은 게임이라면 상관 없겠지만, 26개나 되는 엔딩의 경로가 이리저리 꼬여 있고, 겹치는 부분도 있기 떄문에, 새로 게임을 시작할 때마다 그 넓은 맵들을 반복해야 할 때는 짜증이 날 때가 많다. 이외에도 맵 디자인이 난해하다는 점, 괴물에게 너무 쉽게 잡힌다는 점이 아쉽다. 아마 이 점은 아마추어 개발자인 이상 전문적인 피드백을 많이 받지 못해서 그런 게 아닌가 싶은데, 이후 작품들에서는 고쳐졌으면 좋겠다. 
 
 두 번째 문제는 이 게임에 세이브 장소가 있으나, 생각만큼 쓸모있지 않다는 것이다. 작중에서 조사를 하다 보면 "아드레날린"이라는 것을 주는데, 괴물에게 잡혔을 때 이 아드레날린을 사용하면 세이브 장소에서 다시 시작할 수 있으나, 사용하지 않으면 리스타트를 하게 된다. 문제는 아드레날린은 줍게 되면 이후 회차에서 다시는 등장하지 않기 때문에, 다 쓰고 나면 사용할 수가 없는데, 괴물에게 자주 잡히는 게임 특성상 무한 리겜을 하게 되는 불상사가 발생한다...

 세 번째는 너무 많은 엔딩인데, 다양한 엔딩은 좋지만 각 엔딩의 경로가 서로 꼬이고, 겹치는 경우가 많아서 역시 또 잦은 리겜을 유발한다... 특정 엔딩은 공략을 보지 않고서는 깰 수 없을 정도로 사소하거나 난해한 경로를 가지기 때문에, 이 점 역시 아쉬운 부분이다. 주인공의 아파트가 가진 기괴한 비밀들과 다른 인물들의 이야기를 알아가는 것도 하나의 요소인데, 이게 그 26개의 다른 경로 사이에 걸쳐있기 때문에 두서가 없이 튀어나오고, 이해할 수 없는 경우도 많다. 가장 큰 문제는 이 게임이 아직 미완성이다;; 26개 중 22개만 접근 가능하며, 나머지는 업데이트로 추가한다는데, 유료로 작품을 낸 이상 조금 무책임하지 않은가 싶다.

 이 게임이 정말 아쉬운 이유는, 정말 다양한 아이디어가 사용되었고, 공을 많이 들였다는 게 보이기 때문이다. 대부분의 대사에 음성 녹음(아마 Patreon을 쓴  것 같은데)을 더하고 수많은 일러스트들을 사용해서 지루하지 않게 만들었고, 엔딩에서도 다른 곡들이 사용되는 등 노력을 많이 했다는 것이 느껴진다. 하지만 아쉬운 레벨 디자인과 인터페이스가 너무 큰 단점으로 작용한다. 다른 작품들을 아직 플레이하진 않았지만, 많은 발전이 필요할 것 같다. (그래도 개발자님 응원하는 마음에서 추천드립니다)

2. [i]Red Haze[/i] is a curious game.
It kind of jump-ropes between the supernatural horror genre and a much more credible human horror element.
You take the role of Rockette, who embarks on a quest to score more for her spoon and lighter with a visit to the enigmatic Auntie G.

Your protagonists, Rockette and Starry, are done in a charming artstyle that clashes jarringly against the pencil-whipped horrors you encounters who are drawn in a manner reminiscent of the Underground Galleries of Yume Nikki and .flow; exaggerated features and proportions and scratchy artistic stylings.

The supernatural elements present, I find, take a backseat in [i]Red Haze,[/i] with the sincerest horror elements coming from its human element and unabashed approach to fear, filth, nudity, addiction, murder, and vulnerability: 
The disgust of scrubbing out a vomit-caked bath-tub is sincere. 
The helplessness of waking-up naked in a freezer full of meat is disconcerting.
The discomfort of stepping around the (presumed) dead body of a (presumed) fellow addict slumped in the parking-lot is unnerving and tragic.

[i]Red Haze[/i] isn't perfect, but it is capable of producing a sincere uneasiness. And its realest monsters are human beings that come to life with their surreal depictions and the world's the undertones of sexuality, loss, addiction, lawlessness, and uncleanliness.

Nonlinear and surreal story elements from AestheticGamer / Dusk Golem will have you second-guessing the integrity of your few happy endings and the talented artwork of Rincs adds a depth of visual storytelling you don't typically get with Indie Horror titles. I recommend [i]Red Haze[/i] even in its mostly-complete state. Updates [i]do[/i] occur and there is readily so much to experience.

Red Haze is an indie surprise of the last year. It is incredibly original and somehow really addicting, while it is able to create its own mythology and setting without stealing ideas from other horror games (maybe just a little from Silent Hill, but who doesn't). And if you look in STEAM between the hundreds of uninspired copies of P.T. and Amnesia, you will have an idea of how much a rare quality this is right now. The game is really harsh, mature and disturbing, so surely it is not for everybody.

The game is build on trial and error, but in an effective way. Red Haze right now has around 20 different endings and multiple replays are necessary to discover everything. Some endings are very straightforward and the player can obtained them in few minutes of gameplay, or just by failing. However, other endings are incredibly difficult not only to achieve, but also to just figure how to get them.

The atmosphere is interesting, disturbing and innovative. A constant sense of uncomfortable dread will always follow the player around, while exploring the bizarre and surreal guts of this abandoned building. Every new room is a terrible and disturbing surprise, a new grotesque character or an unexpected enemy. 

Red Haze is a really unique game, with a personal mythology and an interesting concept for an intense and fresh surreal-horror experience. It draw inspiration from very few things, creating something very unique and self-referenced. The game is long and always enriched with new and interesting discoveries. If you are not afraid of a bit of repetitiveness and a rough art-style, Red Haze is a game that can really surprise you.

Red Haze - это хоррор. Хоррор про коллекционирование концовок, коих аж 26 штук. Самые первые концовки можно получить буквально после 5 минут игры. В большинстве своем многие концовки трагические, и напоминают сцены смерти несчастной девочки из игры demonophobia. Кстати, достаточно много деталей роднит Red Haze c той игрой. Повышенная жестокость к женским персонажам, обноженка иногда с самоцензурой, всемогущие жуткие ебаки от которых нужно прятаться, простенькие загадки и около-анимешная стилистика. И стоит упомянуть, что некоторые действия и концовки влияют перманентно на следующие игровые сессии, так что это немного скрасит переигрывание одного и того же.

Если кратко про сюжет, то эта игра про девушку-наркомана, которая ищет себе новую дозу, но находит неприятности.  И по атмосфере игра немного похожа на silent hill: игра не торопится объяснять что происходит в апартаментах, почему некоторые персонажи исчезают сами по себе, происходит постоянное изменение реальности и тд. Историю некоторых персонажей частично объясняют соответсвующие концовки, а другие являются живыми метафорами для главной героини. Как мне кажется. 

Кстати, это еще и спин-офф к игре [url=http://store.steampowered.com/app/377330/Close_Your_Eyes_Old_Version/]Close your eyes[/url](игра бесплатна). Сюжет этой игры так же не совсем понятен, но можно познакомиться с некоторыми персонажами, которые будут присутствовать в этой игре.

Что у игры получается делать, так это пугать. Представьте, что после определенной концовки, маньяк-уборщик, который постоянно преследует главную героиню вдруг исчезает и вы начинаете слышать безумный смех.... "Почему все поменялось?" - этот вопрос вы будете частенько задавать себе. Эта игра пугает непостоянством и своим звуковыми эффектами. Конечно, игра иногда опускается до обычных "БУ" моментов, но в основном предпочитает медленно и размеренно протягивать к вам свои мертвые, белые руки.

В плане механики здесь все просто. Передвижение, сбор предметов и их автоматическое использование на других ключевых предметах. Если в начале ты изучаешь местность и используешь логику, чтобы пройти дальше/получить новую концовку, то чуть позже ты сталкиваешься с совершенно неочивидными вещами. Чтобы получить одну концовку, нужно увеличить свой счетчик морали(?) до определенного уровня(спасибо прохождениям из стим-комьюнити). Этот счетчик никак не показан, про него нет упоминание нигде в игре. Еще есть такой момент, что ты заводишь генератор в подвале и нажимаешь какую-то кнопку в параллельном мире и..... ничего не происходит. На самом деле, нужно еще раз пережить одну из концовок и тебя выбросит на новую локацию. Где здесь логика? Почему после этих действий одна из "концовок" оказалось продолжением игры? Игра бывает иногда совершенно неочевидной.

Огромный минус этой игры в том, что приходится каждый раз повторять одни и те же однотипные действия. И кроме того вам частенько придется пересматривать некоторые катсцены. Причем многие нельзя пропускать. Ситуацию исправило бы частое сохранение, но вот ирония заключается в том, что после прохождения концовки, игра не разрешает загружать старое сохранение. Приходится начинать каждый раз сначала. 

Проблем еще добавляют и монстры. Ладно бы они просто убивали персонажа, так еще к этому блокируется последний файл сохранения. Конечно, есть шприцы адреналина, которые ты ищешь по комнатам. Они по идее позволяют переместиться к последней точке сохранения. Но их всего 12 штук. На всю игру. То есть сохраняться имеет смысл только первые 12 раз, дальше можете пропускать все эти бочки (там где ты сохраняешься). Еще плюс адреналина в том, что он убирает уборщика-маньяка с локации и можно спокойно исследовать локацию. Но это распстраняется только на этого монстра, так что что услугами горящих бочек можно пользоваться только когда хочешь сделать перерыв. В остальном сохраняться смысла не имеет.

В итоге, я склоняюсь к тому, что игру рекомендую. Постоянные переигрывания, бесполезные сохранения почти перевесили все достоинства игры. Большая часть моих 12 часов, которые я наиграл были бессмысленной тратой времени, но игра все же сильно увлекает, особенно в начале. Если вы любите запутанные сюжетные игры завязанные на загадках и изучении местности, но не боитесь всех перечисленных неудобств, то можете попробовать этот бюджетный инди-тайтл.

Questo titolo è stata una rivelazione . Ho sempre adorato il genere horror , in ogni usa forma , e da tempo cerco e colleziono avidamente quelle opere (film , videogiochi etc) che mi facciano effettivamente provare "orrore" , una sensazione che nella nostra quotidianità è quasi impossibile provare( per fortuna aggiungerei) . Eppure questo giochino , all'apparenza uno dei tanti horror-puzzle game in 2D , me l'ha fatta provare . Più che definirlo banalmente come un videogame lo defnirei come "esperienza": non ci ho speso ore perchè mi divertiva , ma perchè mi disturbava , mi incuriosiva e mi coinvolgeva . 

C'è poco da dire sulla trama , che verrà rivelata sempre più ad ogni run : quel poco che ci è dato sapere all'inizio è che vestiamo i panni di una ragazza tossicodipentente , che vive da senzatetto in un complesso abitato abbandonato e il cui unico desiderio a breve termine è quello di raccattare un'altra dose , da brava drogata . Fine . Per avere altri dettagli sulla vita della protagonsita e sul luogo in cui si trova bisognerà giocare una partita dopo l'altra , esplorare i vari scenari e provare raggiungere le varie ending(alcune davvero ostiche), in modo da svelare via via parti sempre più importanti della trama . Ed è proprio questa che mi ha fatto davvero appassionare a red haze : la creatività e l'immaginazione che c'è dietro ad un lavoro del genere è da lodare , il concetto di orrore e terrore viene sviscerato e trattato nella sua purezza . A far paura non sono i morti viventi , i vampiri  o roba simile , a far paura sono principalmente gli esseri umani , o almeno una parte di loro : quella oscura e animale che tutti noi teniamo repressa nel profondo del cuore .. come fosse una specie di belva incatenata . Non che manchino i "mostri" , ma questi sono intesi nel vero senso della parola , cioè come un qualcosa che ci incute terrore e paura : non hanno quindi forme particolarmente definite  , sembrano più le immagini distorte che ci inseguono negli incubi . Non capiamo bene cosa siano .. però ci disturbano , sono raccapriccianti e fuori dal nostro controllo . L'unica cosa che possiamo fare è starne alla larga . Forse è proprio questo che vuole essere red haze , la metafora di un incubo . 

Per concludere , poco mi interessa del gameplay e del comparto tecnico (comunque azzeccatissimo , secondo me , per il tipo di gioco) . Questo non è un gioco per chi cerca meccaniche complicate e grafica da paura , questa è una piccola perla nel panorama horror, una dimostrazione di immensa creatività da parte degli sviluppatori che hanno sicuramente una grande "esperienza" nel genere . Lo consiglio quindi a chi non vuole semplicemente divertirsi a rilassarsi , ma cerca un'esperienza in grado di fargli provare sensazioni contrastanti , che lo confonda , lo coinvolga nelle vicissitudini della protagonista e lo porti a riflettere sulle "zone scure" della natura umana.

TL;DR THIS IS A VERY GOOD AND UNIQUE HORROR GAME 
The PROS of this game definitely outweigh the cons.  I absolutely love that there are more than 20 endings to get; it gives the game a lot of replay value.  I also love the fact that aside from dialogue and comments made by the player character, there is a bigger story that you need to piece together by playing the game again and again, each time uncovering different secrets.  The premise is very original, as you play a drug-addicted squatter in an abandoned apartment building navigating her way to her dealer's room to get more rocks.  I also love the art style and the controls.  Would be super convenient if she could sprint forever, but that would nullify one of the game's main scare mechanisms.  Another thing that I really liked is that while this game is mainly a third person adventure/psychological horror, it does incorporate survival horror elements here and there, which are good for keeping you on your toes!  The game has frightened me to the point of being afraid to play it alone.  The sound effects are also on point.  
The cons, albeit few, are still there, for sure.  Yes, I understand the point of having some playthroughs that are 5 minutes in length and others that can be upwards of an hour.  But many times you accidentally get the same ending because of the aforementioned limited sprint time, which is fine, except for the fact that it does not allow you to return to your last save and makes you restart from the very beginning.  Imagine spending an hour collecting secrets and items and building up for a new ending, and then you accidentally get caught and get the same ending you've gotten several times before and all of that work went to waste.  Other than that, though, the only thing I didn't like very much was the voice acting, but it certainly did it's job and it is subjective.  

Also, I'm not sure if this is a mac thing or if my computer just sucks, but I've had issues with lighting and contrast.  There were certain parts of the game where it was so dark that I could barely make out certain objects, which I thought was just an aesthetic horror touch, until I played the game on my friend's Windows computer, on which everything could be made out clear as day.  I mainly play it on his computer now, for that reason.  

Overall, I would honestly give this game a 9/10.  I hate first person survival horror and am not fond of first person games in general.  This game is different from most horror games I've played and accomplishes its goal extraordinarily well.

EDIT: Regarding my dissatisfaction with losing saves after dying, collecting/hoarding adrenaline makes this a non-issue if you know what you're doing.  It is frustrating that the game has been out for several years and still isn't finished, but I know that when it is, it will be incredible.  So far, I've gotten every single possible ending (on a friend's computer, hence the short playtime), and I can feel the game finally coming to a close.  I can't wait to finish this masterpiece.

But, that being said, I love this game. In fairness I have a soft spot for RPG Maker games and games like them. (Ib, Yume Nikki, OFF and 7th Stand User are my favorites.)

Red Haze goes the extra mile in several departments.

The first thing that springs to mind is the voice acting, most RPG Maker games don't do this cause it can be a a make or break thing. (You don't want your game to sound like House of the Dead 2.) But thankfully, the people they chose for this game are quite talented and fit the characters quite well. Rockette and Starry especially. 

The artwork is also great, the in-game artwork is a lot better than the off-model art in the title card. The character design is very well done without being overdesigned and the monster design does its job at being nightmare inducing. (The eye-scratching ending comes to mind.)



The horror in the game very well done, and harkens back to old PS1 horror like Clock Tower. Encounters in the game are very well designed in that they bring a sense of paranoia. The most of the rooms in which the Custodian appears are dimly lit, so most of the time you won't know which direction he's coming from. And unlike the Clock Tower games, where a change in music was your cue to start running, the only indication that the Custodian is close is that unsettling laugh of his. All these factors together provide a satisfying challenge, and very interesting design choices when you take the time to examine them.


The story so far is very engaging. With a simple premise that becomes complex as the game progresses. Our protagonist is Rockette. A young adult who is also a drug addict. She begins wandering the abandoned apartment building inhabited by druggies, homeless people, and for some reason, creatures. In search of Aunti G a woman who can provide her with a new supply of drugs, it is established early on that Rockette has some kind of history with this woman, no specific details are provided at the start, but it is heavily implied to be nothing good. 
Along the way, Rockette meets a naive but well meaning girl named Starry. They apparently have met before. Upon meeting her, Rockette, and in turn, the player, is given several options. But they boil down to either letting her come with you or leaving her to fend for herself in an abandoned apartment complex. 

In several endings, the fate of Starry is left purposefully unexplained. This only adds to the horror as the player is left to wonder what happens to her in these endings.

The recurring motif of abandonment and decay is very well written and effective. I think the one of strongest examples of this theme was a room where you can examine old newspapers from decades ago that are now falling apart and nigh unreadable. 

Earlier, I mentioned how events change depending on which endings you get and how many. For example, you may encounter a short new scene, or unlock an entire new area. You may find a note lying around that displays different text than it did before. 

The music is also great, each piece fits the mood perfectly and whoever does the vocal songs has a superb voice.

The designs of the areas are quite nice, but the area near the begining with all the hallways stuck out to me. The reason for this is because when I was little, my mom would visit a friend who had an office in a building that had wallpaper that looked remarkably similar to the one in the game.

There is also a permadeath mechanic, if you are killed by the enemies, you are either locked into an ending or receive a game over. There is a way around this, throughout the game, you may find Adrenaline, which can be used to escape the aforementioned permadeath. These are not easy to come by, though, so use them wisely and sparingly.

All in All, I highly recommend this game, It's got a great story, great voice acting, great music, superb gameplay and an overall engaging experience that keeps you coming back. I would like to warn you though, if you have Anxiety like I do, you should be careful about playing this, maybe take a break if you aren't feeling well. Take it easy on yourself, please.
